min_criteria.criterion: M1: names added mass per cycle (division mass minus birth mass) as the observable across cells
min_criteria.rationale: The primary observable is dry_mass mean/CV at division under ppGpp perturbation. Added mass per cycle (division minus birth) appears only inside the adder RIVAL description (protein_mass added), not as the hypothesis's own named observable.

min_criteria.criterion: M2: predicts a roughly constant added increment independent of birth size vs a sizer/timer null
min_criteria.rationale: The hypothesis predicts a stable dry_mass set-point with low CV via ppGpp, not a constant added increment independent of birth size. The adder is framed as a rival to be argued against, and no birth-size-conditioned prediction is made.

min_criteria.criterion: M3: states a falsifier (added mass strongly depends on birth size, i.e. sizer or timer)
min_criteria.rationale: The falsifier is about ppGpp perturbation failing to shift dry_mass mean/CV, not about added mass depending on birth size. No sizer/timer discrimination via birth-size dependence is provided.

min_criteria.criterion: M4: design is an isogenic ensemble tracking per-cycle birth/division mass, in-envelope
min_criteria.rationale: The design uses isogenic seeds over 3 generations tracking per-division dry_mass; it references birth/division mass for the adder rival. This part is in-envelope, though the main analysis emphasizes division mass only.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S1: predicts an added-mass-vs-birth-size slope near zero (adder), with a tolerance
stringent_criteria.rationale: No slope prediction of added mass vs birth size is made; the hypothesis frames the adder as a rival and predicts CV of set-point instead.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S2: specifies the regression of added mass on birth size with a CI on the slope
stringent_criteria.rationale: No regression of added mass on birth size with a CI is specified; statistics are Welch t-tests on dry_mass mean and CV ratios.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S3: the prediction discriminates adder from sizer (slope -1) and timer rivals
stringent_criteria.rationale: The design does not use the slope-based discrimination (adder ~0 vs sizer -1 vs timer). It only checks whether added mass CV stays constant under ppGpp perturbation, which does not separate sizer/timer/adder by slope.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S4: conditions on birth size (the isolating variable) rather than only reporting mean size
stringent_criteria.rationale: The primary analysis reports mean/CV of division mass and does not condition on birth size as the isolating variable; birth size is only mentioned in the rival's constant-increment framing.

b.comment: The hypothesis reframes the question mechanistically around ppGpp-mediated growth-rate control rather than the canonical adder phenomenology. The adder is present only as a rival to be argued against, so nearly all criteria—which center on added-mass-vs-birth-size regression and slope discrimination—are unmet. Only M4 passes because the isogenic multi-generation design with per-division mass tracking is in-envelope and could in principle recover birth/division mass. The core operationalization onto added mass conditioned on birth size is absent.

hypothesis.brief:
OPERATIONALIZED HYPOTHESIS (from the Socratic Council):
  Question:   How does a cell keep its size steady across generations without measuring how big it is?
  Claim (H1): E. coli achieves size homeostasis not by directly sensing cell size, but via a ppGpp-mediated growth-rate-coupled control loop: ppGpp concentration tracks the mismatch between ribosome (translational capacity) supply and charged-tRNA (biosynthetic demand), and this mismatch signal indirectly sets the ribosome/protein allocation that determines steady-state mass — so cells never measure size per se, they measure a flux-balance proxy (charged-tRNA fraction) that happens to co-vary tightly with mass accumulation rate, producing convergence of dry_mass to a condition-specific set-point with low across-generation variance (CV ~5-10%) without any explicit size sensor.
  H1: Across generations, isogenic wildtype cells maintain dry_mass at a stable set-point (steady-state mean, CV <= 10% across seeds/generations) via ppGpp-dependent regulation of ribosome_conc and protein_mass, NOT via any direct size-measuring mechanism; disrupting ppGpp signaling (clamping ppgpp_conc away from its regulated dynamic range, or removing its synthetase RelA) should destabilize or shift the dry_mass set-point and inflate its variance, even though no channel in the model directly encodes 'size' as a sensed input.
  H0: dry_mass set-point and its low variance (CV <= 10%) are unaffected by ppGpp perturbation (clamped ppgpp_conc or relA knockout) relative to wildtype/basal — i.e. size homeostasis is achieved by some ppGpp-independent mechanism (or is simply an emergent numerical artifact of the growth law), so disrupting the alarmone system produces no reliable shift in dry_mass mean or variance beyond replicate noise.
  Predicted effect: 
  Falsifier: disconfirm(target='ppgpp_conc/basal', reference='wildtype/basal', channel='dry_mass'); Welch t-test on per-division dry_mass, target(ppgpp clamp 3x) vs reference(wildtype); reject H0 if |t|>=2 AND |effect_pct|>=15% on mean OR CV ratio >=1.5x; additionally require relA_knockout/basal to show |t|>=2 on dry_mass vs wildtype/basal in the SAME direction-consistent sense (destabilized set-point) to confirm ppGpp-dependence rather than clamp-artifact; refuted if If ppgpp_conc/basal shows |t|<2 and |effect_pct|<15% on dry_mass mean and CV ratio <1.2x relative to wildtype/basal, AND relA_knockout/basal also shows no reliable shift (|t|<2), this refutes H1: size homeostasis would be robust to ppGpp perturbation, implying a ppGpp-independent (or non-existent, purely emergent) mechanism
  Rival: Size homeostasis is achieved by a direct 'adder' mechanism keyed to a fixed increment of protein_mass or rna_mass per cycle, independent of ppGpp — the alarmone only modulates growth rate, not the size set-point itself. -> distinguished by: If the adder-mechanism rival is true, protein_mass added per generation (protein_mass at division minus at birth) should stay constant (CV<=10%) even when ppgpp_conc is clamped 3x basal or relA is knocked out — i.e. dry_mass CV stays low despite ppGpp perturbation, contradicting H1's prediction of destabilization.
  Rival: Size control is dominated by ribosome-capacity limits alone (rrna_operon availability), with ppGpp being a downstream readout rather than a causal regulator of the set-point. -> distinguished by: rrna_operon_knockout (reducing ribosome capacity directly, bypassing ppGpp) should produce a comparable or larger shift in dry_mass mean/CV than the ppGpp clamp; if rrna_operon_knockout/basal shows a much STRONGER effect on dry_mass than ppgpp_conc/basal while ppGpp perturbation shows weak/no effect, this favors ribosome-capacity-as-primary-driver over ppGpp-as-causal-signal.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): The simulator's division event detection (division_rate channel) reliably reports per-division dry_mass snapshots consistent across perturbations, so mass-at-division is a valid proxy for the 'size set-point' even though no explicit size sensor exists in the model.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): ppgpp_conc clamping in the envelope produces a sustained, biologically-plausible stringent-like state (not merely a numerical clamp that decouples from downstream ribosome/protein synthesis machinery) — i.e. clamping propagates causally through the modeled regulatory network.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): relA knockout in this model plausibly reduces (rather than eliminates unpredictably) ppGpp synthesis capacity, producing a genuine 'relaxed' phenotype rather than an unrelated fitness defect; if division_rate for relA_knockout drops well below 1 (lethality), we treat that as a confound and interpret CV/mean shifts only among surviving divisions.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): Across 3 generations, transient (first-generation) mass fluctuations from initial conditions are treated as burn-in noise; only generations 2-3 are used for the primary CV/mean statistics, per replicate seed.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): The claim is scoped to E. coli in this static basal medium condition only; extension to other media (e.g. acetate) or to dynamic nutrient shifts is out of scope for this hypothesis and left as future work.

min_criteria.criterion: M1: names per-gene expression as a function of chromosomal (ori-ter) position as the observable
min_criteria.rationale: Operationalizes reporter expression (rna_mass/protein_mass slope) as a function of insertion_locus (near_oriC vs near_ter), explicitly framing expression as a function of chromosomal position.

min_criteria.criterion: M2: predicts origin-proximal genes higher than terminus-proximal at fast growth vs a position-flat null
min_criteria.rationale: H1 predicts oriC > ter at basal fast growth; H0 is the explicit position-flat null of statistically indistinguishable output.

min_criteria.criterion: M3: states a falsifier (no position gradient in expression)
min_criteria.rationale: Falsifier specifies refutation if welch_t<2 or effect_pct<20% at basal (no gradient), among other conditions.

min_criteria.criterion: M4: design compares expression by position across >=1 growth condition (ideally 2), in-envelope
min_criteria.rationale: Design compares oriC vs ter across both basal (fast) and acetate (slow) conditions using in-envelope new_gene perturbation and standard channels.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S1: predicts the gradient strengthens with growth rate, with a rough ori/ter ratio
stringent_criteria.rationale: Predicts +50-100% (1.5-2x) at fast growth shrinking to +10-30% at slow growth, giving a rough ori/ter ratio and growth-rate dependence.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S2: specifies a regression of expression vs position (and vs growth rate) with CIs
stringent_criteria.rationale: Uses paired t-test/Welch t-test on slope differences and stratifies by condition, but does not specify a regression of expression vs position/growth rate with confidence intervals.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S3: the prediction discriminates a replication-dosage bias from position-flat and regulation-only rivals
stringent_criteria.rationale: Rival A (regulation-only, gap persists at slow growth) and H0 (position-flat) are explicitly distinguished by the growth-rate-dependent shrinkage prediction.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S4: contrasts fast vs slow growth (the isolating control that the bias is dosage, not regulation)
stringent_criteria.rationale: Explicitly contrasts basal (fast, multifork-heavy) vs acetate (slow, multifork-minimal) as the isolating control, plus a ppGpp-clamp growth-rate-matched arm.

b.comment: Strong operationalization of the Klumpp-Hwa dosage bias onto ori/ter reporter placement across growth conditions. Correctly flags the position-dependent copy-number assumption as an auxiliary (scope_note satisfied). Only S2 fails: analysis relies on paired t-tests rather than an explicit regression with CIs.

hypothesis.brief:
OPERATIONALIZED HYPOTHESIS (from the Socratic Council):
  Question:   Are genes near where DNA replication starts expressed more than genes near where it ends?
  Claim (H1): In fast-growing E. coli, genes located near the chromosomal origin (oriC) are expressed at higher levels than genes located near the terminus (ter), because during overlapping replication rounds (multifork replication) origin-proximal loci are present in more copies per cell than terminus-proximal loci, so their transcript/protein output scales with local gene dosage. Because the simulator's new_gene insertions are run as separate constructs, we operationalize the comparison as a WITHIN-SAME-SEED-SET paired design (matched seeds/timeline/condition, differing only in insertion_locus), and we explicitly flag as an auxiliary assumption — not an established fact — that the envelope's new_gene mechanism encodes position-dependent copy number for near_oriC vs near_ter insertion_locus values; this is checked downstream, not argued here.
  H1: Origin-proximal reporter genes show higher steady-state expression output (rna_mass/protein_mass accumulation slope, matched-seed paired comparison) than terminus-proximal reporter genes at matched insertion expression strength, with the gap larger at high growth rate (basal, multifork-heavy) and shrinking at low growth rate (acetate, multifork-minimal); the gap must also PERSIST when ppGpp is clamped to hold growth_rate statistically matched across clamp/no-clamp runs, showing it is dosage-driven rather than ppGpp/ribosome-allocation-driven.
  H0: Origin-proximal and terminus-proximal reporter genes show statistically indistinguishable expression output (no dosage-driven gap) across all conditions and under the ppGpp clamp, i.e. any apparent difference is within replicate noise or fully explained by growth-rate/ppGpp allocation rather than chromosomal position.
  Predicted effect: Paired oriC-vs-ter rna_mass/protein_mass slope difference of roughly +50-100% (1.5-2x) under basal (fast growth, growth_rate ~1.5-2/h), shrinking to +10-30% under acetate (slow growth); under the ppGpp clamp restricted to growth_rate-matched seed-pairs, the gap should remain >=40% (largely unchanged from unclamped basal), showing dosage rather than ppGpp-linked allocation drives it.

hypothesis.claim: In fast-growing E. coli, genes located near the chromosomal origin (oriC) are expressed at higher levels than genes located near the terminus (ter), because during overlapping replication rounds (multifork replication) origin-proximal loci are present in more copies per cell than terminus-proximal loci, so their transcript/protein output scales with local gene dosage. Because the simulator's new_gene insertions are run as separate constructs, we operationalize the comparison as a WITHIN-SAME-SEED-SET paired design (matched seeds/timeline/condition, differing only in insertion_locus), and we explicitly flag as an auxiliary assumption — not an established fact — that the envelope's new_gene mechanism encodes position-dependent copy number for near_oriC vs near_ter insertion_locus values; this is checked downstream, not argued here.
hypothesis.h1: Origin-proximal reporter genes show higher steady-state expression output (rna_mass/protein_mass accumulation slope, matched-seed paired comparison) than terminus-proximal reporter genes at matched insertion expression strength, with the gap larger at high growth rate (basal, multifork-heavy) and shrinking at low growth rate (acetate, multifork-minimal); the gap must also PERSIST when ppGpp is clamped to hold growth_rate statistically matched across clamp/no-clamp runs, showing it is dosage-driven rather than ppGpp/ribosome-allocation-driven.
hypothesis.h0: Origin-proximal and terminus-proximal reporter genes show statistically indistinguishable expression output (no dosage-driven gap) across all conditions and under the ppGpp clamp, i.e. any apparent difference is within replicate noise or fully explained by growth-rate/ppGpp allocation rather than chromosomal position.
hypothesis.predicted_effect: Paired oriC-vs-ter rna_mass/protein_mass slope difference of roughly +50-100% (1.5-2x) under basal (fast growth, growth_rate ~1.5-2/h), shrinking to +10-30% under acetate (slow growth); under the ppGpp clamp restricted to growth_rate-matched seed-pairs, the gap should remain >=40% (largely unchanged from unclamped basal), showing dosage rather than ppGpp-linked allocation drives it.

falsifier.decision_rule: Paired Welch t-test (or paired t-test) on per-seed-matched (oriC_slope - ter_slope) rna_mass accumulation differences within basal condition; reject H0 (declare origin>terminus, dosage-driven) only if welch_t>=2 AND mean paired effect_pct>=50%. Require the paired gap to shrink to <=30% in the acetate (slow-growth) condition. Additionally, within the ppgpp_conc=1.0x clamp arm, restrict to growth_rate-matched seed-pairs (growth_rate within 10% between clamp and no-clamp) and require the paired gap there to remain >=40%.
falsifier.refuting_result: welch_t<2 or paired effect_pct<20% at basal, OR the gap fails to shrink under acetate (stays >=50%), OR under the growth_rate-matched ppGpp clamp the paired gap collapses to <20% — any of these would refute a growth-rate-dependent, dosage-driven, ppGpp-independent mechanism.

rivals.claim: Rival A (regulatory, not dosage): any origin-vs-terminus expression difference is driven by local transcription-factor/promoter regulatory context (e.g. supercoiling-sensitive promoters concentrated near oriC) rather than copy number, so the paired gap would persist even at slow growth (acetate) when multifork replication is minimal.
rivals.distinguishing_result: If Rival A is true, the paired origin/terminus gap stays roughly constant (does NOT shrink to <=30%) across basal vs acetate conditions, decoupled from growth_rate/multifork extent — contradicting H1's prediction that the gap tracks growth-rate-dependent dosage.

rivals.claim: Rival B (ppGpp-mediated growth-rate allocation masquerading as a position effect): the apparent origin/terminus gap is actually just growth-rate-dependent global ribosome/RNA-polymerase allocation correlated with which genes were chosen, not true replication-position dosage.
rivals.distinguishing_result: Within the growth_rate-matched ppgpp_conc=1.0x clamp seed-pairs, if Rival B is correct the paired gap collapses toward <20% (because holding ppGpp/growth-rate fixed removes the allocation confound that was masquerading as position); if H1 (dosage) is correct the gap persists >=40% since chromosomal copy number is unaffected by the clamp.

Seed indices are assumed to be drawn from directly comparable stochastic streams across separate runs sharing the same seed_pairing_key, such that seed i's paired trajectories (oriC vs ter) experience matched intrinsic noise realizations for growth/division timing — the closest available proxy to true within-cell dual-reporter isolation, since the envelope does not support two simultaneous reporters in one cell.

min_criteria.criterion: M1: names ribosomal vs catabolic proteome fraction (or ribosome_conc) and growth rate as the observables
min_criteria.rationale: Names ribosome_conc, ribosome/protein_mass ratio, and growth_rate explicitly as observables; though catabolic sector is only gestured at ('stress/scavenging proteins') without per-species reads, ribosome_conc + growth_rate suffice for M1.

min_criteria.criterion: M2: predicts carbon limitation shrinks the ribosomal sector / raises catabolic proteins vs a rich baseline
min_criteria.rationale: Predicts ribosome_conc/protein_mass falls >=25% under carbon downshift vs basal/wildtype reference.

min_criteria.criterion: M3: states a falsifier (allocation unchanged under limitation)
min_criteria.rationale: H0 and decision rule state the shift being indistinguishable/attenuated; though framed around relA_KO gating, the Step-1 requirement (|t|>=2 AND effect_pct<=-25%) establishes the reallocation effect itself, so a null there falsifies.

min_criteria.criterion: M4: design contrasts carbon-limited vs rich conditions across seeds, in-envelope
min_criteria.rationale: Timeline downshift vs wildtype basal at 6 seeds, 4 generations, minimal glucose ramp — in-envelope condition contrast.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S1: states the linear tradeoff (ribosomal fraction falling with limitation) with a rough slope vs growth
stringent_criteria.rationale: Uses growth_rate only as a covariate to argue the ribosome drop is disproportionate to growth; it does NOT state the linear ribosomal-fraction-vs-growth tradeoff or any slope — in fact argues against pure growth-rate coupling.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S2: specifies a sector-fraction comparison across conditions with CIs
stringent_criteria.rationale: Ribosome/protein_mass ratio compared target vs reference with Welch t-test across 6 seeds; effect_pct with statistical test approximates CI-based comparison, though catabolic sector fraction is not separately quantified.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S3: the prediction discriminates a reallocation tradeoff from fixed-allocation and uniform-scaling rivals
stringent_criteria.rationale: Rivals addressed are ppGpp-causal-gating vs growth-rate-dilution vs tRNA-throttle — a mechanism-of-signaling axis. It does not discriminate reallocation-tradeoff from fixed-allocation or uniform-scaling; indeed the Scott-type growth-law rival is treated as the null, and the hypothesis's own H0 concedes the ribosome drop happens even without ppGpp.

stringent_criteria.criterion: S4: collapses conditions onto the growth-rate axis (ribosomal fraction ∝ growth) as the isolating law
stringent_criteria.rationale: Explicitly rejects growth-rate collapse as the isolating law, using growth_rate only as a confound to control against; the ribosomal-fraction ∝ growth relationship is framed as the rival to defeat, not the isolating law.

b.comment: The hypothesis reframes the canonical proteome-allocation question as a mechanistic ppGpp/RelA causal-gating study. It satisfies all minimum criteria (observables, direction, falsifier, in-envelope design) but misses most stringent criteria because it pursues a signaling-mechanism axis (ppGpp-causal vs passive) rather than the Scott/Hui growth-law linear-tradeoff axis. It never states the ribosomal-fraction \u221d growth slope, discriminates against fixed/uniform-scaling rivals, or uses the growth-rate collapse as the isolating law — in fact it treats the growth-law as a rival to be excluded.

hypothesis.brief:
OPERATIONALIZED HYPOTHESIS (from the Socratic Council):
  Question:   When carbon is scarce, how does a cell re-budget which proteins it makes?
  Claim (H1): Under carbon scarcity (glucose ramp-down/cut), E. coli triggers a stringent response in which RelA-dependent ppGpp accumulation drives a coordinated re-budgeting: ribosome synthesis (ribosome_conc, rna_mass) is down-regulated while the cell preferentially maintains/increases relative allocation to stress/scavenging proteins, producing a measurable, ppGpp-causal shift in the ribosome-to-protein-mass ratio rather than a passive consequence of slowed growth alone.
  H1: Carbon downshift causes a RelA/ppGpp-dependent active re-allocation: ppgpp_conc rises >=3-fold above basal within ~1-2 generations, ribosome_conc/protein_mass ratio falls >=25% relative to wildtype/basal at matched timepoint, and this fall is abolished (attenuated to <=10% of the wildtype effect size) when RelA is knocked out — i.e., the re-budgeting is causally gated by ppGpp, not merely a passive dilution effect of reduced growth rate or an independent tRNA-charging-mediated throttle.
  H0: The ribosome/protein re-allocation under carbon downshift is indistinguishable (within noise) between wildtype and relA-knockout backgrounds — i.e., any drop in ribosome_conc or ribosome:protein ratio is a growth-rate-driven passive effect (dilution, translation-rate coupling) or a ppGpp-independent tRNA-charging-mediated throttle, and does NOT require ppGpp signaling; ppgpp_conc changes are epiphenomenal/correlated but not causal.
  Predicted effect: Direction: carbon downshift -> ppgpp_conc rises ~3-5x basal within 2 generations; ribosome_conc/protein_mass ratio falls by >=25% vs wildtype/basal reference at matched generation. Causal gating magnitude: in relA_KO background under the same downshift, the ribosome-ratio drop is attenuated to <=10% of the wildtype effect size (>=90% attenuation), while growth_rate itself still falls comparably (within 20%) across backgrounds. Rival-exclusion magnitude: if the tRNA-charging throttle (not ppGpp) were the true driver, fraction_trna_charged would fall by a similar magnitude (within 20%) in relA_KO as in wildtype AND ribosome ratio would still drop >=20% in relA_KO — this is the outcome that would refute ppGpp-causal gating.
  Operationalize: 'stringent response activation' -> ppgpp_conc (fold-change of ppgpp_conc at generation 2-3 post-shift vs wildtype/basal baseline)
  Operationalize: 'ribosome re-budgeting' -> ribosome_conc and rna_mass relative to protein_mass (ratio ribosome_conc/protein_mass (and rna_mass/protein_mass) at matched generation, compared target vs reference)
  Operationalize: 'growth-rate confound' -> growth_rate (instantaneous growth_rate trace used as covariate to test whether ribosome ratio change tracks growth_rate alone vs is disproportionate)
  Operationalize: 'causal gating by ppGpp' -> ribosome_conc/protein_mass shift in relA_KO background vs wildtype under identical downshift (attenuation ratio: effect_pct(relA_KO shift vs relA_KO basal) / effect_pct(wildtype shift vs wildtype basal))
  Operationalize: 'tRNA-charging-mediated rival throttle' -> fraction_trna_charged (fraction_trna_charged trajectory (gen 1-3) compared wildtype-shift vs relA_KO-shift; test whether tRNA charging falls and ribosome ratio drops in parallel in relA_KO despite blocked ppGpp rise)
  Falsifier: disconfirm(target='timeline/carbon_downshift_wildtype', reference='wildtype/basal', channel='ribosome_conc'); Step 1: Welch t-test of ribosome_conc/protein_mass ratio at generation 3, target vs reference, across 6 seeds each; require |t|>=2 AND effect_pct <= -25% to establish the shift effect. Step 2: compute attenuation_ratio = effect_pct(relA_KO shift vs relA_KO basal) / effect_pct(WT shift vs WT basal). Partition the FULL outcome space with two thresholds only (no gap): attenuation_ratio <= 0.10 supports H1 (ppGpp-causal gating); attenuation_ratio > 0.10 (i.e. >10% of WT effect remains) refutes H1 in favor of H0 -- there is no undefined middle region. Step 3 (rival exclusion): additionally require fraction_trna_charged in relA_KO-shift to drop by <=20% relative to relA_KO-basal (i.e. tRNA charging is NOT independently collapsing) for the ppGpp-gating claim to be credited as the operative mechanism rather than a tRNA-throttle rival.; refuted if relA_KO under the same carbon downshift shows attenuation_ratio > 0.10 (ribosome_conc/protein_mass ratio drop retains more than 10% of the wildtype effect magnitude) despite negligible ppgpp_conc rise, OR fraction_trna_charged collapses similarly in relA_KO and wildtype while ribosome ratio still falls >=20% in relA_KO -- either result indicates the re-allocation is growth-rate/dilution or tRNA-throttle driven, not ppGpp-causally gated.
  Rival: Passive dilution/growth-rate coupling: ribosome content simply tracks growth rate via a universal growth-law relationship (Scott et al.-type), independent of ppGpp signaling per se. -> distinguished by: relA_KO background under carbon downshift still shows the same ~25%+ drop in ribosome_conc/protein_mass ratio as wildtype (attenuation_ratio > 0.10), tracking growth_rate decline 1:1, with no attenuation despite blocked ppGpp rise.
  Rival: Post-transcriptional/translational throttling via charged-tRNA sensing at the ribosome (ppGpp-independent), with ppGpp rise being a correlated but non-causal marker. -> distinguished by: fraction_trna_charged drops sharply (>=20% relative fall) and ribosome_conc/protein_mass falls similarly (>=20%) in relA_KO as in wildtype under downshift, showing the tRNA-charging/translation-feedback loop alone reproduces the ribosome reduction without needing ppGpp elevation.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): The simulator's timeline mechanism for a glucose ramp/cut is mechanistically wired to trigger amino-acid/carbon starvation signaling (uncharged-tRNA accumulation) rather than being purely a media-label switch with no downstream physiological cascade.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): relA_knockout in this simulator meaningfully reduces ppGpp synthesis without independently ablating unrelated stress pathways (spoT-mediated ppGpp synthesis/hydrolysis is treated as a background constant not confounding the comparison); we no longer rely on a ppgpp_conc clamp arm as the causal control since its mechanistic equivalence to blocked RelA signaling was not justifiable -- relA_KO alone is the primary discriminating control, run both under downshift and under basal to compute the attenuation ratio cleanly.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): protein_mass and rna_mass aggregate channels are fine-grained enough to detect a 25% shift in ribosome allocation against overall biomass changes within 4 generations.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): Stochastic seed-to-seed variability (isogenic noise) at 6 seeds is sufficient to resolve a 25% effect size via Welch's t; if not, this is treated as a power limitation rather than evidence against H1.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): We do not attempt to resolve deterministic-chaos vs intrinsic-noise contributions to seed variance; per-seed spread is reported but not decomposed further.
  Assumes (ceteris paribus): fraction_trna_charged is assumed to be a valid proxy for the rival's proposed ppGpp-independent translational-feedback signal in this simulator.

instantaneous growth_rate trace used as covariate to test whether ribosome ratio change tracks growth_rate alone vs is disproportionate

operational_defs.observable: ribosome_conc/protein_mass shift in relA_KO background vs wildtype under identical downshift
operational_defs.measure: attenuation ratio: effect_pct(relA_KO shift vs relA_KO basal) / effect_pct(wildtype shift vs wildtype basal)
fraction_trna_charged trajectory (gen 1-3) compared wildtype-shift vs relA_KO-shift; test whether tRNA charging falls and ribosome ratio drops in parallel in relA_KO despite blocked ppGpp rise

assumptions: The simulator's timeline mechanism for a glucose ramp/cut is mechanistically wired to trigger amino-acid/carbon starvation signaling (uncharged-tRNA accumulation) rather than being purely a media-label switch with no downstream physiological cascade.

relA_knockout in this simulator meaningfully reduces ppGpp synthesis without independently ablating unrelated stress pathways (spoT-mediated ppGpp synthesis/hydrolysis is treated as a background constant not confounding the comparison); we no longer rely on a ppgpp_conc clamp arm as the causal control since its mechanistic equivalence to blocked RelA signaling was not justifiable -- relA_KO alone is the primary discriminating control, run both under downshift and under basal to compute the attenuation ratio cleanly.
protein_mass and rna_mass aggregate channels are fine-grained enough to detect a 25% shift in ribosome allocation against overall biomass changes within 4 generations.

Stochastic seed-to-seed variability (isogenic noise) at 6 seeds is sufficient to resolve a 25% effect size via Welch's t; if not, this is treated as a power limitation rather than evidence against H1.
We do not attempt to resolve deterministic-chaos vs intrinsic-noise contributions to seed variance; per-seed spread is reported but not decomposed further.
fraction_trna_charged is assumed to be a valid proxy for the rival's proposed ppGpp-independent translational-feedback signal in this simulator.
